comment: Real-world applications the indexer is validated against. Fixtures prove a
construct is handled; this corpus proves the handling survives contact with
code nobody wrote for us — vendored directories, generated files, dialects,
`rev` pins an exact commit so a run is reproducible; bump it deliberately.
Expectations are FLOORS, not equalities: a corpus repo that grows must not
break the build, but one where detection collapses must. Count floors sit at
roughly 70% of the values measured at the pinned commit; `min_resolution_pct`
sits 10 points under its measured value. They are REGRESSION detectors, not
quality bars — a repo whose architecture defeats static resolution (Rails
autoloading, MediatR indirection) carries an honestly low floor with the
scripts/fetch-corpus.sh --report prints the current measurements and the

repos.name: express-realworld
repos.why: Express + Prisma REST API in TypeScript, with a Jest suite. Resolution is low (27%) because the handlers are thin wrappers over Prisma's generated client, which is not in the tree.

repos.name: django-realworld
repos.why: Django REST Framework: class-based views, routers, urls.py routing. Ships no tests — a zero here is correct, and guards against a detector that invents them.

repos.name: gin-realworld
repos.why: Gin router groups plus a real _test.go suite.

repos.name: spring-petclinic
repos.why: The canonical Spring Boot app: @GetMapping controllers, JUnit 5.

repos.name: laravel-realworld
repos.why: Laravel routing + Eloquent. Its PHPUnit suite is written in the docblock style (`/** @test */` over snake_case methods), so it also guards the comment-annotation path — and its bundled public/js/app.js guards against reading RegExp `.test()` as a Jest case.

repos.name: rails-realworld
repos.why: Rails routes.rb + controllers. Its test/ tree is untouched scaffolding (every case commented out), so zero cases is the correct answer here too. KNOWN GAP: with Zeitwerk autoloading there are no imports to follow, so only ~3% of Ruby call sites resolve and no route links to a controller action; the floor records the gap rather than hiding it.

repos.name: aspnetcore-realworld
repos.why: ASP.NET Core attribute routing + MediatR, xUnit suite (16 [Fact]s, all found at the pinned commit). Resolution is low (19%) by design of the app: nearly every call goes through MediatR's `_mediator.Send(command)` indirection, which no static resolver can follow.

repos.name: axum
repos.why: Large Rust workspace: #[test]/#[tokio::test] at scale, plus routes declared across hundreds of examples.

repos.name: googletest
repos.why: The gtest macros in their native habitat — thousands of TEST/TEST_F, plus Python unittest runner scripts alongside them.

repos.name: bats-core
repos.why: Bash at scale plus a large .bats suite — the bats detection's home turf.

repos.name: vapor
repos.why: Server-side Swift: protocol-heavy code, and a suite mid-migration from XCTest to Swift Testing — both idioms live in the same tree.

repos.name: afnetworking
repos.why: Objective-C at scale: categories, blocks, XCTest.

repos.name: ktor-samples
repos.why: Kotlin DSL routing across many small apps — Ktor route detection, and a polyglot tree (Kotlin, Swift, JS, Bash) that must not bleed between languages.
